name: CocoRosie
label: Touch and Go
lede: Two sisters who hadn't spoken in years made a record in a Paris bathroom with toy pianos and one microphone, and Touch and Go talked them out of giving it only to friends.

eras.title: Reunion in a Montmartre bathroom
eras.text: The Casady sisters grew up on the move across Hawaii, Arizona, California and New Mexico, then barely spoke for a decade. Bianca's surprise visit to Sierra's Paris flat in 2003 turned into a record neither of them planned to sell.

years.h: Bianca turns up unannounced at Sierra's flat in Paris
years.p: Sierra Casady was in Paris training as an opera singer; Bianca Casady was in Brooklyn. Bianca told Clash the near-silence of ten years had been their choice, not distance.
years.xp:
Sierra had studied voice in Rome, then at the Manhattan School of Music and Mannes, before moving into a tiny Montmartre apartment in 2000 for the Conservatoire de Paris. She later admitted how she got in: "I pretended I could sight-read when I couldn't."

Bianca had been running a small press and book clubs out of her home in New York. The visit was meant to be short. It lasted months.

years.h: Twelve songs cut in the bathroom, the flat's best-sounding room
years.p: The sisters record on one microphone and a broken pair of headphones, over toy pianos, harps and found objects. They picked the bathroom because it was the most isolated room in the apartment.

years.h: La maison de mon rêve comes out on Touch and Go
years.p: The sisters wanted a few copies for friends. Touch and Go wanted the record, and Pitchfork gave it a 6.9.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says the label pursued them and persuaded them. The sisters later told Kaput that [[TV on the Radio|eb872766-98f6-453d-883f-2ae908a18315]]'s Dave Sitek "had a role in getting us signed," and that they slipped into a small New York scene that included [[Anohni|90cc2464-234e-4da0-b39b-576f36e633bc]] and [[Devendra Banhart|0110e63e-0a9b-4818-af8e-41e180c20b9a]].

The UK release followed on April 12, 2004. Jon Beasley of Hecuba helped with the layout.

years.h: A racial slur on "Jesus Loves Me" draws fire
years.p: Wikipedia notes that Sierra Casady uses the slur six times on the debut's "Jesus Loves Me." Sierra said she found it shocking anyone was offended.
years.xp: Bianca Casady defended the song in 2016, saying creative work should "not always be politically correct" and that a writer should be able to explore "the racist perspective."

years.cap: CocoRosie with Antony on tour, November 2004
years.h: Toy instruments at the Islington Academy, opening for Antony
years.p: CocoRosie share a London bill with Antony, now [[Anohni|90cc2464-234e-4da0-b39b-576f36e633bc]]. The Guardian loved the records and found the live show too pleased with itself.
years.xp: David Peschek's review called the recordings "dreamlike, strange and entirely intoxicating," then wrote that the sisters "could learn a little about restraint" on stage, surrounded by garish plastic toys.

eras.title: Unicorns, a farm in the Camargue, a Pierre et Gilles cover
eras.text: The second and third records were made on the move and at their mother's farm in Saintes-Maries-de-la-Mer, with friends from the New York freak-folk crowd dropping in. The covers got as much attention as the songs.

years.h: Noah's Ark, with Anohni on piano and Banhart on a cell phone
years.p: Anohni sings and plays on "Beautiful Boyz," a song about Jean Genet; Devendra Banhart phones in his vocal on "Brazilian Sun"; French rapper Spleen opens "Bisounours."
years.xp: It was recorded wherever the sisters stopped: a field by the road, a barn in the south of France, a studio in Brooklyn, Sierra said. Metacritic scored it 67 from 24 reviews.

years.cap: Bianca and Sierra Casady in Bologna, July 2005
years.h: Bianca's unicorn drawing lands on a worst-covers list
years.p: Pitchfork's November 2005 list of the worst record covers ever includes the Noah's Ark sleeve: Bianca's drawing of three unicorns, one throwing up the colors of the spectrum. The Guardian named it again in 2007.

years.h: Prada's spring 2006 runway walks to CocoRosie
years.p: Sound designer Frédéric Sanchez builds a Prada show soundtrack from "Brazilian Sun," "Good Friday" and "Not for Sale," calling the piece "Coco Rosie Through the Looking Glass."

years.cap: CocoRosie with Devendra Banhart at Sous la plage, Paris
years.h: Bianca and Devendra Banhart move in on her mother's farm
years.p: In 2005 Banhart lived with Bianca Casady and her mother at the farm in Saintes-Maries-de-la-Mer. They split in 2006, and Uncut reported that his 2007 album Smokey Rolls Down Thunder Canyon detailed the breakup.

years.cap: Sierra and Bianca Casady at Les Eurockéennes, Belfort
years.h: A label, a gallery on Ludlow Street, and Sierra's Metallic Falcons
years.p: Bianca starts Voodoo Eros Records with Melissa Shimkovitz and opens the Voodoo Eros Museum of Nice Items at 123 Ludlow St. The label puts out Metallic Falcons, Sierra's side project with Matteah Baim.

years.h: Ghosthorse and Stillborn, begun in a barn by a graveyard
years.p: Started in a barn on their mother's Camargue farm, finished with [[Björk|87c5dedd-371d-4a53-9f7f-80522fb7f3cb]] collaborator [[Valgeir Sigurðsson|b47171a4-1bfc-4d80-a91e-33c368fa6a5a]]. Some songs are about people buried in the farm's old graveyard, children among them.
years.xp:
Their older half-brother Simon Casady died on May 5, 2006, and their grandfather later that month, during production; Wikipedia says the songs deal with the family. Friends Tez and Spleen beatbox on several tracks.

Pierre et Gilles shot the cover: Sierra twice, in Victorian dress, and Bianca as a kneeling soldier. Metacritic averaged 60. "Rainbowarriors" drew criticism for borrowing a New Age "Rainbow Warriors" legend presented as Native American.
play: The Adventures of Ghosthorse and Stillborn

years.h: The rest of the North American tour is cancelled
years.p: Partway through the Ghosthorse tour, the remaining North American dates are called off. No official explanation was released.

eras.title: Five countries, then Sub Pop
eras.text: With no new album for three years, the sisters wrote in Buenos Aires, Melbourne, Berlin, New York and Paris. When the record came, it came out on Sub Pop, and Touch and Go's run with them was over.

years.h: Bianca wonders why nobody mentions the drag
years.p: Bianca Casady regularly performs in a fake mustache and appears as a man in the "Rainbowarriors" video. She told AfterEllen she was surprised so few people notice, or realize she is queer.
years.xp: She contrasted it with Anohni, who she said was "torn apart" in early press. Her own drag, she said, went mostly unremarked.

years.h: "God Has a Voice, She Speaks Through Me" on a 3,000-copy picture disc
years.p: The single comes out digitally and as a limited 7-inch picture disc. Its B-side is an untitled track made mostly of noises.

years.cap: CocoRosie's Transhumance performance at the Centre Pompidou, Paris, April 2009
years.h: Coconuts, Plenty of Junk Food, sold only at the merch table
years.p: A self-released EP goes on sale exclusively at CocoRosie shows. By then, Wikipedia says, their relationship with Touch and Go had become unclear.

years.h: Off Touch and Go and onto Sub Pop for Grey Oceans
years.p: The February announcement of the album confirmed the label move. "Undertaker" carries a recording of their mother, Christina Chalmers, singing what turned out to be a Cherokee translation of "Amazing Grace."
years.xp: The final version was recorded in five countries. Pitchfork's Ian Cohen called CocoRosie "one of the world's biggest cult acts" and the album their least abrasive yet; the BBC went after the cover's "energy crystals, faux-facial hair" and typography. "Lemonade" reached No. 74 in France.

years.h: A week after Grey Oceans, the sisters play Berlin
years.p: The tour takes the new songs to one of the cities where they were written.

years.cap: Bianca Casady's Nightshift, Donaufestival, Krems, April 2012
years.h: Bianca stages Nightshift at Donaufestival in Krems
years.p: At the Austrian festival, Bianca Casady presents a performance piece of her own, separate from the band's set.

years.cap: Ticket for CocoRosie at the Royal Festival Hall, Meltdown festival, London, 2012
years.h: "We Are On Fire" brings them back to Touch and Go for one 7-inch
years.p: The double A-side single, recorded with Dave Sitek of [[TV on the Radio|eb872766-98f6-453d-883f-2ae908a18315]] and featuring Antony Hegarty, comes out on Touch and Go.

eras.title: Their own label and their mother's last session
eras.text: CocoRosie scored Robert Wilson's stage productions, started their own label and kept recording at the farm. Their mother, whose voice is on Grey Oceans, died during the sessions for the seventh album.

years.h: Tales of a GrassWidow on City Slang, with Sigurðsson back
years.p: Metacritic averages 75 from 18 reviews, and Pitchfork called it "remarkably straightforward" next to what came before.

years.cap: Sierra Casady at Traumzeit Festival, June 2013
years.h: Robert Wilson hires them for Peter Pan at the Berliner Ensemble
years.p: The first of several scores for the director: Pushkin's Fairy Tales in Moscow (2015), Edda in Oslo (2017) and The Jungle Book in Luxembourg (2019) followed.

years.h: Heartache City, first release on their own Lost Girl Records
years.p: Back to a 4-track approach at the farm studio, with toys from suitcases dating back to the La maison days. Bianca announced her solo project, Bianca Casady and the C.i.A., the next month.

years.src: Wikipedia: CocoRosie · Wikipedia: Put the Shine On
years.h: Christina Chalmers dies eleven days after singing on "Ruby Red"
years.p: The sisters' mother, an artist and Waldorf teacher who gave them the nicknames Coco and Rosie, sings backing vocals on a song about her own life, then dies during the album sessions.

years.h: "Smoke 'em Out" with Anohni, written for the Women's March
years.p: A protest song against Donald Trump's election, released days before the inauguration. The same day they confirm work has begun on Put the Shine On.

years.h: The sisters work on Chance the Rapper's The Big Day
years.p: Their time on [[Chance the Rapper|373a4c98-a46b-48e4-86ec-f6ca65b4f438]]'s album feeds the heavier hip-hop sound of the record they were finishing.

years.h: Put the Shine On, made in San Francisco and on a Hawaii ranch
years.p: Songs were tried out at their brother Nathan's ranch on the Big Island. Pitchfork gave it a 5.1, and Cracked criticized "Hell's Gate" for borrowing from slave songs.

eras.title: After the fire
eras.text: A forest fire took the family house and everything in it. Twenty years in, the sisters stripped old songs down to piano and voice, then made a loud record for a new label.

years.h: A forest fire burns the Casady family house
years.p: Bianca said the fire took their mother's artwork, the family photographs, their instruments, recording gear and costumes. Insurance covered the house but not the studio, so they started a GoFundMe, NME reported.

years.h: Twenty years on, the hits go back to piano and voice
years.p: For the anniversary, unplugged shows including one at HAU Hebbel am Ufer in Berlin, and the Elevator Angels EP, with pianist Gael Rakotondrabe back in the fold.
years.xp: They chose songs that suited piano and voice and leaned toward the most popular ones, they told Kaput, because they wanted to give something to the fans, "which isn't generally the way we roll." In October, "Least I Have You" arrived with Deerhoof's Greg Saunier sitting in.

q: It's trashy and sexy and dark and pretty upbeat
years.h: Little Death Wishes on Joyful Noise, with Chance the Rapper
years.p: The eighth album brings in Rakotondrabe on piano, [[Deerhoof|11eabe0c-2638-4808-92f9-1dbd9c453429]]'s Greg Saunier on percussion and Chance the Rapper. OndaRock says Sierra wrote most of the words.
